passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
Come on — everybody's doing it. That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good — drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world.

Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. In South Africa, an HIV-prevention initiative known as loveLife recruits young people to promote safe sex among their peers.

The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the lameness of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. "Dare to be different, please don't smoke!" pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers — teenagers who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues convincingly that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure.

But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological mechanisms that make peer pressure so powerful. Now and again, the author glimpses the truth: that the flaw of the social cure is that it cannot provide a long-lasting cure. It doesn't work very well for very long. The trouble with Rage Against the Haze is that the funded billboard campaigns and events will not be sustained forever; indeed, in South Carolina, the number of young smokers rebounded after state funding was cut. Meanwhile, in South Africa, evidence that loveLife produces lasting changes is limited and mixed.

There's no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits — as well as negative ones — spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we unconsciously imitate the behavior we see every day.

Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It's like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that's the problem with a social cure engineered from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
A deal is a deal — except, apparently, when Entergy is involved. The company, a major energy supplier in New England, provoked justified outrage in Vermont last week when it announced it was reneging on a longstanding commitment to abide by the state's strict nuclear regulations.

Instead, the company has done precisely what it had long promised it would not: challenge the constitutionality of Vermont's rules in the federal court, as part of a desperate effort to keep its Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant running. It's a stunning move.

The conflict has been surfacing since 2002, when the corporation bought Vermont Yankee and negotiated an agreement with state regulators to keep the products moving. The plant was scheduled to open up in 2012, and Entergy offered to apply for state permission if it wished to keep the plant open longer. But Entergy went further: Entergy agreed that it would need the legislature's approval. Then, too, the company went along.

Either Entergy never really intended to live by those commitments, or it underestimated the Vermont public's resistance to nuclear power. A string of accidents, including a partial collapse of a cooling tower in 2007 and the discovery of underground tritium leakage in 2010, raised serious questions about the plant's safety and Entergy's management. The Senate in Vermont voted 26 to 4 last year against allowing an extension.

Now the company is suddenly claiming that the 2002 agreement is invalid because of the 2006 legislation, and that only the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has the authority to determine whether the plant is safe enough to operate and whether its license should be extended. But if the company had kept its word, that debate would be beside the point.

The company seems to have concluded that its reputation in Vermont is already so damaged that it has nothing left to lose: By suing the state, it has admitted that it would rather take its chances with a federal judge than with the state's regulators, but it has also lost any claim to being an honest broker in Vermont. As Entergy sells its nuclear power across New England, it will likely find that Vermont is not the only state that will keep in mind what promises from Entergy are worth.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by the objective researcher using the scientific method to carry out work. But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route. We aim to be objective, but we can never completely escape the context of our unique life experience. Prior knowledge and interests influence what we experience, what we think our experiences mean, and the actions we take, so that the opportunities for misinterpretation, error, and self-deception abound.

Consequently, discovery claims should be thought of as protoscience. Similar to newly staked mining claims, they are full of potential. But it takes collective scrutiny and acceptance to transform a discovery claim into a mature discovery. This is the credibility process, through which the individual researcher's me, here, now becomes the community's anyone, anywhere, anytime. Objective knowledge is the goal, not the starting point.

Once a discovery claim becomes public, the discoverer receives intellectual credit for having made it. But the claim does not get accepted as fact until it gets confirmed. Usually this requires that other researchers try to duplicate the findings and that subsequent research cannot be made until the findings are confirmed. In the process, the original claim gets modified, broadened, and made more specific, as other researchers adapt it to their own purposes and contexts. In other words, a discovery claim works its way through the community, the idea is revised, its value tested, and its boundaries defined.

Two paradoxes exist throughout this credibility process. First, scientific work tends to see itself as a solitary pursuit, but discovery is essentially a collective act. Second, the very nature of science is to doubt, yet discovery requires belief. For a discovery claim to be accepted, other scientists must believe in the honesty and competence of the discoverer, while simultaneously remaining skeptical of the claim itself.

In the end, credibility "happens" to a discovery claim — a process which can take weeks, months, or even years. Annette Baier has described this process as "the creation of trust between strangers who share a common commitment to the truth." As Albert Szent-Gyorgyi put it: "Discovery consists of seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought." Through this collaborative crucible, provisional claims are transformed into established knowledge.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
If the trade unionist Jimmy Hoffa were alive today, he would probably represent civil servants. When Hoffa's Teamsters were in their prime in 1960, only one in ten American government workers belonged to a union; now 36% do. In 2009 the number of unionists in America's public sector passed that of their fellow members in the private sector. In Britain, more than half of public-sector workers but only about 15% of private-sector ones are unionized.

There are three reasons for the public-sector unions' thriving. First, they can shut things down without suffering much in the way of consequences. Second, they are mostly bright and well-educated. A quarter of America's public-sector workers have a university degree. Third, they now dominate left-of-centre politics. Some of their ties go back a long way. Britain's Labor Party, as its name implies, has long been associated with trade unionism. Its current leader, Ed Miliband, owes his position to votes from public-sector unions.

At the state level their influence can be even more fearsome. Mark Baldassare of the Public Policy Institute of California points out that much of the state's budget is patrolled by unions. The teachers' unions keep an eye on schools, the CCPOA on prisons and a variety of labor groups on health care.

In many rich countries average wages in the state sector are higher than in the private one. But the real gains come in benefits and work practices. Politicians have repeatedly "backloaded" public-sector pay deals, keeping the pay increases modest but adding to holidays and especially pensions that are already generous.

Reform has been vigorously opposed, perhaps most notoriously in education, where charter schools, academies and merit pay all faced drawn-out battles. Even though there is plenty of evidence that the quality of the teachers is the most important variable, teachers' unions have fought against getting rid of bad ones and promoting good ones.

As the cost to everyone else has become clearer, politicians have begun to clamp down. In Wisconsin the unions have rallied thousands of supporters against Scott Walker, the hardline Republican governor. But many within the public sector suffer under the current system, too.

John Donahue at Harvard's Kennedy School points out that the norms of culture in Western civil services suit those who want to stay put but is bad for high achievers. The only American public-sector workers who earn well above $250,000 a year are university sports coaches and the president of the United States. Bankers' fat pay packets have attracted much criticism, but a public-sector system that does not reward high achievers may be a much bigger problem for America.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Think of those fleeting moments when you look out of an aeroplane window and realize that once, not so long ago, to look in this way was the province of only the gods and the birds. But having been thrilled by the astonishing sense of flight on our early journeys around the world, we now seem to treat it as entirely ordinary: an annoyance that takes up time, rather than an event that opens the mind.

The second half of the 20th century saw a collection of geniuses, warriors, entrepreneurs and visionaries labour to create a fabulous machine that could function as a typewriter and printing press, studio and theatre, paintbrush and gallery, piano and radio, the mail as well as the mail carrier. [41] ________

Anyone who has ever worked at an office desktop or curled up with a laptop in bed might be forgiven for thinking that the computer has finally fulfilled that promise. But the true significance of the computer is still emerging. [42] ________

But for all the reasons there are to celebrate the computer, we must also be on our guard. Today, we are in danger of being seduced into a culture of consumption rather than production: of downloading other people's culture rather than creating our own.

All animals download, but only a few upload. Beavers build dams and birds make nests. Yet for all the reasons there are to celebrate the computer, only humans make culture: they do so by translating their experiences into music, paintings, books and other creations, and then sharing them with others. [43] ________

Yet for all the possibilities of our new culture machines, most people are still stuck in download mode. Even after the advent of widespread social media, a pyramid of production remains, with a small number of people uploading material, a slightly larger group commenting on or modifying that content, and a huge percentage remaining content to just consume. [44] ________

For all the possibilities of our new culture machine, television is still the medium that shapes the world's culture. Television is a one-way tap: you open the valve and information flows out. [45] ________

What counts as meaningful uploading? My definition revolves around the concept of "stickiness" — creations and experiences to which others adhere, which make a lasting impression on other people's minds and give them reason to think, feel or create something of their own.

[A] Of course, it is precisely these superfluous things that define human culture and ultimately what it is to be human. Downloading and consuming culture requires great skills, but failing to move beyond downloading is to strip oneself of a defining constituent of humanity.

[B] Applications like tumblr. com, which allow users to combine pictures, words and other media in creative ways and then share them, have the potential to add stickiness by amusing, entertaining and enlightening others.

[C] Not only did they develop such a device but by the turn of the millennium they had also managed to embed it in a worldwide system accessed by billions of people every day.

[D] This is because the networked computer has sparked a secret war between downloading and uploading — between passive consumption and active creation — whose outcome will shape our collective future in ways we can only begin to imagine.

[E] The challenge the computer mounts to television thus bears little similarity to one format being replaced by another in the manner of record players being replaced by CD players.

[F] One reason for the persistence of this pyramid of production is that for the past half-century, much of the world's media culture has been defined by a single medium — television — and television is defined by downloading.

[G] The networked computer offers the first chance in 50 years to reverse that flow, to encourage thoughtful downloading and, even more importantly, meaningful uploading.

【精准定位】最后一段①句首先提出质疑：专家和官僚们能否成功挑选我们的同伴群体并将其引导至道德方向还远不能确定（Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select...）；②③句通过老师调换捣蛋学生座位的类比说明该策略从未真正奏效（The tactic never really works）；④句指出从外部人为调控的根本问题所在：现实中我们坚持自己选择朋友。由此可见，作者对同侪压力在社会治疗中的效果持怀疑态度，［D］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［D］questionable是对第六段中far less certain、never really works、the problem with a social cure等表达所体现的作者怀疑态度的精准提炼。

【错项排除】［A］利用④句the problem捏造出“同侪压力本身是有害的”，而原文旨在说明外部调控存在问题；［B］利用①句virtuous捏造“令人满意的”，与作者全段批驳基调相悖；［C］利用第五段①句exert enormous influence过度引申出“深刻的”，偏离了末段对人为调控效果的质疑主旨。

由此可以看出，作者对于 peer pressure 的影响持质疑态度，故答案选 D。

questions.stem: The phrase "reneging on" (Line 3, Para. 1) is closest in meaning to ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】由第一段首两句可知：协议就是协议，但Entergy公司显然是个例外（A deal is a deal — except, apparently, when Entergy is involved）。该公司宣布它将reneging on一项遵守该州严格核法规的长期承诺，激起了公众合理的愤怒。由此推知，该公司做出了违背承诺的行为，故该短语意为“违背，背信”，［C］dishonoring正确。

【命题解密】正确项［C］dishonoring（不尊重，不履行，违背）是基于首句A deal is a deal以及provoked justified outrage对reneging on所做的精准同义替换。

【错项排除】［A］condemning谴责；［B］reaffirming重申；［D］securing获得，确保。均与上下文关于“毁约、背弃承诺”的语境不符。

questions.stem: By entering into the 2002 agreement, Entergy intended to ________.

options.text: seek favor from the federal legislature
options.content: seek favor from the federal legislature

options.text: acquire an extension of its business license
options.content: acquire an extension of its business license

options.text: get permission to purchase a power plant
options.content: get permission to purchase a power plant

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第三段①句明确指出：这一冲突自2002年起就已表面化，当时该企业收购了佛蒙特扬基核电站，并与州监管机构达成协议（when the corporation bought Vermont Yankee and negotiated an agreement with state regulators to keep the products moving）。Entergy公司签订该协议的目的是为了获得收购该核电站的许可，故［D］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［D］get permission to purchase a power plant是对第三段①句bought Vermont Yankee and negotiated an agreement with state regulators的合理概括。

【错项排除】［A］将达成协议曲解为寻求州监管机构的“保护”；［B］将州议会批准曲解为寻求“联邦立法机构的支持”；［C］将2002年购买协议与后来2012年寻求许可证延期混淆，属于张冠李戴。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, Entergy seems to have problems with its ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段②句明确指出：接二连三发生的事故，包括2007年冷却塔部分倒塌以及2010年发现地下氚泄漏，引发了对该核电站安全性以及Entergy公司管理水平的严重质疑（raised serious questions about the plant's safety and Entergy's management）。故［A］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［A］managerial practices是对第四段②句Entergy's management的同义替换。

【错项排除】［B］将冷却塔倒塌和管道泄漏等安全与管理事故曲解为“技术创新”问题；［C］“财务目标”和［D］“商业远见”在文中均未提及，纯属无中生有的干扰项。

questions.stem: In the author's view, the Vermont case will test ________.

options.text: Entergy's capacity to fulfill all its promises
options.content: Entergy's capacity to fulfill all its promises

options.text: the nature of states' patchwork regulations
options.content: the nature of states' patchwork regulations

options.text: the federal authority over nuclear issues
options.content: the federal authority over nuclear issues

options.text: the limits of states' power over nuclear issues
options.content: the limits of states' power over nuclear issues

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第五段②句指出：法律学者认为该案将对各州核监管权限提供一个测试性先例；③④句作者进一步指出：明确各州权限虽会引起对拼凑法规的合理担忧，但Entergy公司的毁约行为使得联邦法院不得不去界定州级核监管权限（the limits of state regulatory power）。故［D］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［D］the limits of states' power over nuclear issues对应第五段末句the limits of state regulatory power。

【错项排除】［A］将测试州监管权限偷换为Entergy公司履行承诺的能力；［B］将担忧州补丁法规偷换为检验其“性质”；［C］将州政府在核能问题上的权力界限曲解为联邦权力，主体混淆。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that ________.

options.text: Entergy's business elsewhere might be affected
options.content: Entergy's business elsewhere might be affected

options.text: the authority of the NRC will be defied
options.content: the authority of the NRC will be defied

options.text: Entergy will withdraw its Plymouth application
options.content: Entergy will withdraw its Plymouth application

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】最后一段末句明确指出：由于Entergy在整个新英格兰地区销售核电，它很可能会发现，佛蒙特州绝非唯一一个把Entergy承诺的信誉价值牢记在心的州（As Entergy sells its nuclear power across New England, it will likely find that Vermont is not the only state that will keep in mind what promises from Entergy are worth）。这暗示其背信弃义的行为将影响其在其他地区的业务，故［A］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［A］是对末句“佛蒙特州绝非唯一一个记住其承诺价值的州”的合理推论引申。

【错项排除】［B］将NRC会记住Entergy的信誉曲解为NRC的权威将被藐视；［C］撤回申请与［D］佛蒙特州名誉受损均与原文事实相反，名誉受损的是Entergy公司而非佛蒙特州。

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, the process of discovery is characterized by its ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第一段②句明确指出：在日常科学实践中，科学发现往往遵循一条模糊且复杂的路径（But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route）。因此［A］正确。

【命题解密】题干the process of discovery与正确项［A］uncertainty and complexity分别同义替换原文discovery follows an ambiguous and complicated route。

【错项排除】［B］将影响科研过程的主观因素（先验知识、误解自欺）曲解为科学发现过程本身的特征；［C］将理想状态下的特点（objective）偷换为现实状态的特征；［D］系统性与规律性属于常识干扰，背离第一段强调的复杂性与模糊性。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 2 that credibility process requires ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第二段③句指出：科学发现声明转变为成熟发现需要经过集体的审查与认可（takes collective scrutiny and acceptance）；④句进而指出：单个研究者的“我、此时、此地”由此转变为科学界的“任何人、任何时间、任何地点”。由此可推知取信过程需要集体的共同努力，［B］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［B］shared efforts对应第三句collective scrutiny and acceptance以及第四句community's anyone, anywhere, anytime。

【错项排除】［A］将集体审查狭隘化为严格的单向检查；［C］强调“个人智慧”，与原文反复强调的集体行动（collective scrutiny/community）截然相反；［D］“持续创新”在文中未体现。

questions.stem: Paragraph 3 shows that a discovery claim becomes credible after it ________.

options.text: has attracted the attention of the general public
options.content: has attracted the attention of the general public

options.text: has been examined by the scientific community
options.content: has been examined by the scientific community

options.text: has received recognition from editors and reviewers
options.content: has received recognition from editors and reviewers

options.text: has been frequently quoted by peer scientists
options.content: has been frequently quoted by peer scientists

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第三段指出：发现声明在得到证实之前不能被作为事实接受，这通常需要其他研究人员复制结果，声明在科学共同体中历经检验、修正、测试其价值并明确其界限（a discovery claim works its way through the community, the idea is revised, its value tested, and its boundaries defined）。故［B］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［B］has been examined by the scientific community是对第三段全段所述同行重复实验、修正和检验过程的全面概括。

【错项排除】［A］吸引公众注意力并非确立可信度的必要条件；［C］将整个科学界同行的检验偷换为期刊编辑和审稿人个别环节；［D］被同行引用在第三段中并未作为可信度成立的判定标准。

questions.stem: Albert Szent-Gyorgyi would most likely agree that ________.

options.text: efforts to make discoveries are justified
options.content: efforts to make discoveries are justified

options.text: scientific work calls for a critical mind
options.content: scientific work calls for a critical mind

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第五段引述Albert Szent-Gyorgyi的名言：“科学发现就是见众之所见，思无人之所思”（Discovery consists of seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought）。这表明科学工作需要不落俗套、独立思考与批判性思维，故［D］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［D］scientific work calls for a critical mind是对引语thinking what nobody has thought的深度内涵概括。

【错项排除】［A］、［B］、［C］脱离了Albert Szent-Gyorgyi具体引语关于思维独创性与批判性的核心内涵，属于偏离引语主旨的泛泛之论。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title of the text?

options.text: Novelty as an Engine of Scientific Development.
options.content: Novelty as an Engine of Scientific Development.

options.text: Evolution of Credibility in Doing Science.
options.content: Evolution of Credibility in Doing Science.

options.text: Challenge to Credibility at the Gate to Science.
options.content: Challenge to Credibility at the Gate to Science.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】文章首段指出科学发现充满主观复杂性；第二段引出核心概念“取信过程”（credibility process）；第三段阐述发现声明在学术共同体中经历的修改与检验；第四段剖析取信过程中的两大悖论；末段总结可信度如何在共同体协作中最终确立。全文主线始终围绕“科学研究中可信度的演进与确立”，故［C］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［C］Evolution of Credibility in Doing Science涵盖了全文的核心主题词credibility与发展过程evolution。

【错项排除】［A］以偏概全，误将新颖性作为全文主旨；［B］集体审查仅是取信过程中的一个手段，不足以概括全文；［D］中心词落于“挑战”，脱离了阐释科学如何克服主观因素确立客观可信度的行文主轴。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the first paragraph that ________.

options.text: Teamsters still have a large body of members
options.content: Teamsters still have a large body of members

options.text: Jimmy Hoffa used to work as a civil servant
options.content: Jimmy Hoffa used to work as a civil servant

options.text: unions have enlarged their public-sector membership
options.content: unions have enlarged their public-sector membership

options.text: the government has improved its relationship with unionists
options.content: the government has improved its relationship with unionists

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第一段指出：1960年美国政府工作人员中只有十分之一加入工会，而如今达到36%；2009年公共部门工会会员人数超过了私营部门；英国一半以上的公共部门人员也加入了工会。这表明工会极大地扩大了其在公共部门的会员人数，故［C］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［C］是对第一段数据对比（10%到36%，公共部门超过私营部门）的概括性同义替换。

【错项排除】［A］文中仅提及Teamsters在1960年全盛时期的情况，无法推知现在的会员状况；［B］对首句虚拟语气断章取义，Jimmy Hoffa并非公务员；［D］“政府改善了与工会成员的关系”与文意无关。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of Paragraph 2?

options.text: Public-sector unions are prudent in taking actions.
options.content: Public-sector unions are prudent in taking actions.

options.text: Education is required for public-sector union membership.
options.content: Education is required for public-sector union membership.

options.text: Labor Party has long been fighting against public-sector unions.
options.content: Labor Party has long been fighting against public-sector unions.

options.text: Public-sector unions seldom get in trouble for their actions.
options.content: Public-sector unions seldom get in trouble for their actions.

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第二段②句指出公共部门工会壮大的第一个原因：他们可以举行罢工使全国运转瘫痪而无须承担太多后果（they can shut things down without suffering much in the way of consequences）。由此可知，他们很少因为自己的行动而陷入麻烦，故［D］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［D］seldom get in trouble for their actions同义改写原文without suffering much in the way of consequences。

【错项排除】［A］称其行动谨慎，与可以随时罢工瘫痪运转相反；［B］将四分之一拥有大学学位曲解为工会会员资格有教育硬性要求；［C］将工党与工会渊源久远且领袖得益于工会选票曲解为工党长期与工会斗争，完全颠倒黑白。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 4 that the income in the state sector is ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】第四段③句指出：政治家们反复采取变相延期给付的方式制定公共部门薪酬协议，保持工资涨幅微弱，但增加假期、尤其是原本就已经非常优厚的养老金（keeping the pay increases modest but adding to holidays and especially pensions that are already generous）。这表明公共部门的收入通过隐蔽、间接的方式得到了增加，故［B］正确。

【命题解密】题干与正确项［B］indirectly augmented是对原文backloaded pay deals以及增加假期与养老金福利的精准概括。

【错项排除】［A］政治家与工会达成的协议并非“非法获得”；［C］工资涨幅保持modest（低微），并非过度增加；［D］这种变相给付加重了纳税人负担并拖累财政，并非“公平调整”。

questions.stem: The example of the unions in Wisconsin shows that unions ________.

options.text: often run against the current political system
options.content: often run against the current political system

options.text: may be a barrier to public-sector reforms
options.content: may be a barrier to public-sector reforms

questions.explanation:
【精准定位】根据题干关键词Wisconsin定位到第六段，该段实际接续第五段（段落主旨句①句）文意“公共部门改革遭到工会强烈反对”：段首指出由于当前不合理体制的代价越来越明显，政治家们已开始采取强硬措施（进行改革），随后提及威斯康辛州各工会集结大批支持者反对州长（政治家之一）。可见，作者意在借此例说明工会阻碍了应有的公共部门改革。［C］正确。

【命题解密】第六段承接第五段而来，因此第六段中事例论证实际是出现于第五段首句的观点。［C］是第五段首句 Reform has been vigorously opposed（by the trade unions）的同义改写。

【错项排除】［A］将第六段②句渗透之意一“工会反对意在改革现行体制的州长，以维护现有体制”反向曲解为“工会反对现行政治体制”；［B］与［D］将该句渗透之意二“工会召集成千上万的支持者反对强硬的州长”分别曲解为“工会能够改变人们的政治态度”、“工会在政府内占据主导地位”。

【技巧总结】面对“事例写作目的题”，考生应：理清行文脉络、区分论点论据，体味事例以点带面的性质。具体解答思路为：①圈定“事例范围”并将其做为一个整体加以理解，并从上下文中寻找作者“观点结论”或“意在说明的现象”，注意搜索范围不是“段”，而是“意群”（有时需跨段寻找）；②注意正确项特征：不仅能完整概括事例，还需明显大于事例本身，且能和上下文顺滑衔接，成为一体；③了解干扰项设置方式：直接摘取文中细枝末节；歪曲事例中具体细节；扭曲论点（事例说明对象）。具体到本题为：先根据关键词the unions in Wisconsin定位到第六段②句，并进而将事例讲述范围扩大到①②句，将事例本身大致概括为“威斯康辛州工会集合力量反对州长行动”。然后向上段寻找论点/事例说明对象，发现明显观点句为 Reforms has been vigorously opposed（by unions），而［C］（unions） may be a barrier to public sector reforms和该句近义，且体现了事例以点带面的性质，故确定为正确项。

questions.stem: John Donahue's attitude towards the public-sector system is one of ________.
questions.explanation:
【精准定位】末段引述哈佛大学肯尼迪学院John Donahue的观点：西方行政体制的文化规范适合那些追求安稳的人，但对优秀人才不利（suit those who want to stay put but is bad for high achievers）；一个不能奖励优秀人才的公共部门体制对美国来说可能是个大得多的问题。由此可见其对现行体制持强烈的批评否定态度，故［A］正确。

【命题解密】正确项［A］disapproval（不赞同，反对）精准概括了专家言论中的is bad for high achievers以及a much bigger problem。

【错项排除】［B］appreciation欣赏；［C］tolerance容忍；［D］indifference漠不关心。均与专家鲜明的批判态度不符。
